opinions.name: Orca
opinions.point: lovely tool for hands-on guided coding
opinions.quote: I use a lot of Opencode + Deepseek, strategize some of that work with Claude Opus… When I guide by hand I use Orca Dev, which is lovely.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: GitHub-issue handoff is simple and resilient
opinions.quote: Claude drops GitHub issues that Opencode picks up on a schedule. It’s simple and resilient enough for me.

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: core tech, stable where OpenClaw crashed
opinions.quote: Hermes Agent, which has become a core tech for me. I’ve tried to use Openclaw but… It spirals and crashes after a week in ways I’ve never experienced from Hermes, doing the same things.

opinions.name: OpenClaw
opinions.point: couldn't keep it running; spirals and crashes weekly
opinions.quote: I’ve tried to use Openclaw but it has not been something I can keep running. It spirals and crashes after a week in ways I’ve never experienced from Hermes

opinions.name: Chat UI (web/app)
opinions.point: remembers context well, but opaque when working locally
opinions.quote: Claude Projects is pretty nice and integrates with Claude Artifacts for design tasks… My only gripe is that it's really intransparent when Claude works locally.

opinions.name: Muse
opinions.point: only 1-2 prompts per window, but unlimited turns
opinions.quote: [Muse Code] has a 5 hour usage limit, and if using the wonder model, you basically only get 1 or 2 prompts. However, I find it will basically do unlimited 'turns', so as long as I give a good prompt, I can get my work done.

opinions.name: OpenClaw
opinions.point: wasted scarce tokens
opinions.quote: I tried openclaw but found it a waste of my already scarce tokens. :D I build my own runners when I need a loop or cron-based automation.

opinions.name: Muse
opinions.point: unused for months, probably cancelling
opinions.quote: Muse Code ($12?) - probably cancel Muse Code since I haven't touched it in a few months

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: hasn't found many use cases for it
opinions.quote: [I run] a small qwen model on a second laptop for hermes (mostly searching and summarization tasks)… hermes: can't find a lot of use cases right now

opinions.name: Gemini
opinions.point: cheap for what you get, but stingy tokens
opinions.quote: I use Gemini Pro and anti gravity completely out of the box. And am not super pleased, but it is also quite cheap for what you get… I also think that Argon-tokens are super stingy.

opinions.name: Antigravity
opinions.point: endlessly digs through git history after small changes
opinions.quote: If I tell [Antigravity] to make a change in layout to a page and there is a "collateral" change, I cannot tell it to "change that back", because it will spend an hour digging through git history diffing stuff that is not related in any way.

opinions.name: MLX
opinions.point: local MLX models hold up for everything
opinions.quote: things i run locally using apple mlx models: general llm, coding llm, text-to-image, text-to-video, image-to-video, text-to-music, everything is holding up well.

opinions.name: Custom harness
opinions.point: switching subscriptions mid-session is very productive
opinions.quote: I use xAI and OpenAI subscriptions, switching between them, even mid session, using my Lunar harness… This is a very productive setup for me.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: $20 plan rarely runs out of tokens
opinions.quote: I have $20 subscription for both [Claude and Codex]… I mostly use weaker models on lower effort… I am rarely out of tokens so I do not plan to pay more.

opinions.name: ChatGPT / Codex
opinions.point: $20 plan rarely runs out of tokens
opinions.quote: I have $20 subscription for both [Claude and Codex]… I mostly use weaker models on lower effort… I am rarely out of tokens so I do not plan to pay more.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: plan rates much better than API rates
opinions.quote: I pay for claude ultra coz the plan rates are significantly better than the api rates, and i feel like i can tokenmax harder than if i am constantly watching my credit balances.

opinions.name: OpenRouter
opinions.point: Nemotron available, but Gemma free models rate-limited
opinions.quote: openrouter free models, usually nemotron coz they have decent availability and I don't get constantly rate limited like with the gemma models on there.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: Slack lets them talk to agents where they work
opinions.quote: something custom, i wired it all up in slack so i could easily talk to agents through the same place i do my work

opinions.name: OpenClaw
opinions.point: not transparent enough for autonomous development
opinions.quote: Used to use openclaw on a raspberry pi to experiment with like autonomous development but i needed something with a bit more transparency so i moved everything into slack.

opinions.name: DeepSeek
opinions.point: $50 lasts forever for small stuff
opinions.quote: Deepseek for non-important stuff, 50 bucks seems to last forever… I only use it for small stuff, mostly as a way to validate API use on some implementations.

opinions.name: Gemini
opinions.point: solid complement when Claude usage runs out
opinions.quote: Gemini 20 buck a month sub to complement Claude when i run out of usage. There is some kind of extra Argon allowance at the moment, so it's pretty solid.

opinions.name: Custom harness
opinions.point: full app-building harness, fun to build
opinions.quote: I built railvio.com for myself… it’s a full harness for building applications + fully integrated Jira and Confluence clone… It’s been super fun building everything.

opinions.name: Pi
opinions.point: their harness of choice, wholeheartedly
opinions.quote: I generally use open weight models (Kimi K3.1, Mistral Large 4, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek v4.1 Flash…)… [For a coding harness:] Pi all the way.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: yolo mode on a dedicated server is pleasant
opinions.quote: I'm running [Claude Code] almost exclusively on a dedicated server… I let it run there in yolo mode, which is pleasant to work with. I found this the easiest way to sandbox the LLM, and am quite happy with it so far.

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: Codex app is awesome, better than TUI
opinions.quote: with codex, the app is just awesome, don't use the tui (its good, but the app is better). Claudes app sucks in comparison

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: Claude's app sucks compared to Codex's
opinions.quote: with codex, the app is just awesome… Claudes app sucks in comparison, though is often better than the TUI.

opinions.name: Dots
opinions.point: coordinates lots of side-hustle work
opinions.quote: dots, It's kind of like a project manager for the side hustle, its really coordinating a lot of stuff between all the things I have in flight

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: prefers its project and session creation
opinions.quote: I use both [the Codex and Claude apps] as well, but I find them fairly interchangeable. I like project and session creation a bit more on codex.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: good model and aesthetics, but TUI poor fit
opinions.quote: I do not like terminal tui much as I think it's a poor fit for a coding agent. But I do use claude code tui because I have a sub: it is a good model and I like its aesthetics.

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: great model for local development
opinions.quote: I run Qwen 3.8 27B NVFP4 with ninfer on my 5090. It's a great model for local development.

opinions.name: Custom harness
opinions.point: custom harness on Claude sub works with cache
opinions.quote: I built a custom harness that uses my Claude subscription… I even pass it custom tools as args and it works with the cache, and you can even append messages to conversations

opinions.name: Dots
opinions.point: helpful as a workload dispatcher
opinions.quote: [I use the] Default CLI most of the time, plus some agent-made tooling for some orchestration… I'm using Dot, and I find it helpful as a workload dispatcher

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: vibe-coded control room is very productive
opinions.quote: I've built a web-based control room for a single developer to run multiple agents from multiple vendors behind a single pane of glass… Completely vibe-coded (Ruby on Rails), but very productive.

opinions.name: Fizzy
opinions.point: async kanban delegation feels like a colleague
opinions.quote: I use a locally running instance of Fizzy kanban board to manage and track all work… In general feeling more like working with a colleague than chatting with a bot.

opinions.name: Subagents (built-in)
opinions.point: spawned subagents implement features end to end
opinions.quote: more Opus, Sonnet, Astra, and Sol (sometimes also Grok) subagents are spawned for the actual implementations. This is really powerful and often implements features completely e2e with proper verification and testing etc.

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: keeps sensitive health and finance data local
opinions.quote: My local qwen model can dual serve chat and decisions on the same weights. I mainly use chat here for critical data like health & finance topics that I'm not comfortable sending to a provider I don't control

opinions.name: Custom harness
opinions.point: fills gaps like multi-account usage draining
opinions.quote: I built Caudra, a custom harness / coding agent that fills many gaps I otherwise had to build with various plugins… For instance, multi account support with strategies such as draining the sub account that hits reset soonest.

opinions.name: Custom orchestration
opinions.point: very useful, improves as models improve
opinions.quote: I've built my own custom system including web UI which helps me manage agents powered by claude and codex… It's proving very useful, and keeps getting better as models improve.

opinions.name: OpenClaw
opinions.point: tried it but it didn't stick
opinions.quote: I've built my own custom system including web UI which helps me manage agents… [As for broader agent platforms,] I tried OpenClaw but it didn't stick for me

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: $200 plan doesn't raise weekly limits; burns usage
opinions.quote: I have two $100/mo Anthropic accounts (watch out the single $200 doesn't raise weekly limits)… letting Claude control that tends to burn my usage too quickly anyway

opinions.name: Gemini
opinions.point: Argon hallucinates, but better than Opus for SwiftUI
opinions.quote: Argon hallucinates, so I rarely use it for impl, but I've actually had better results with it than Opus for SwiftUI and AppKit work.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: already incredibly productive with plain Claude Code
opinions.quote: I feel like I'm just scratching the the surface with AI coding but am already incredibly productive. My setup is purely Claude Code Max (£90/month) within PHPStorm's terminal view.

opinions.name: OpenClaw
opinions.point: falls apart when given real work
opinions.quote: Used previously OpenClaw and Hermes but it seems to fall apart when you give it any real work. Ending up giving up because I just don't have to tinker / fine-tune it.

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: falls apart when given real work
opinions.quote: Used previously OpenClaw and Hermes but it seems to fall apart when you give it any real work. Ending up giving up because I just don't have to tinker / fine-tune it.

opinions.name: Muse
opinions.point: enjoyable for personal things
opinions.quote: I will say, I enjoy Muse a lot for some reason for personal things. I don't overshare anything I wouldn't mind saying in public.

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: just works for backend, but sucks at design
opinions.quote: I basically use Claude Design exclusively for front end work and Codex for backend work. Codex just works but sucks as design.

opinions.name: Claude
opinions.point: great at design but can't finish anything
opinions.quote: I basically use Claude Design exclusively for front end work… Claude is great at design (with enough references) but can't seem to actually get anything to completion.

opinions.name: T3 Code
opinions.point: great app for remotely controlling any harness
opinions.quote: Now I hardly open my laptop. T3 on the phone (great app for remotely controlling any harness) Which connects to my tiny home server

opinions.name: GitHub Copilot
opinions.point: reviewer catches things cheap models miss
opinions.quote: [My setup is] T3->Opencode->Openrouter… Copilot reviewer catches some things in my PRs that openrouter on cheap misses.

opinions.name: GitHub Copilot
opinions.point: mishandles reasoning models in Visual Studio
opinions.quote: I really want to use 6.1 Terra, but the way copilot is set up in visual studio proper, they don't handle reasoning models correctly (or maybe my install is screwed up).

opinions.name: OpenAI API
opinions.point: trusts paid API tokens over subsidized ones
opinions.quote: I prefer (pre) paying for tokens… I'll still never believe that those subsidized tokens are always the same as the ones I get through the API.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: recent models token efficient enough
opinions.quote: I use Claude and codex and use my own orchestrator to run them. I also used to have open code for a while but the recent codex and Claude models are token efficient so don’t need additional models.

opinions.name: Codex
opinions.point: recent models token efficient enough
opinions.quote: I use Claude and codex and use my own orchestrator to run them. I also used to have open code for a while but the recent codex and Claude models are token efficient so don’t need additional models.

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: local models too dumb and too slow
opinions.quote: I’ve experimented with Qwen locally but the models that run on my hardware are too dumb for extended use cases and too slow for quick questions.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: eats tokens too fast for personal use
opinions.quote: I use employer paid Claude Code in the day job but it eats tokens at a rate I’m not willing to pay for for personal use.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: uninspiring security track record
opinions.quote: I’ve tried OpenCode but their security track record is uninspiring and I’m way more defensive about my personal hardware than my employer is

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: chosen for model satisfaction
opinions.quote: Claude Code + Custom Harness(set of skills) + Mod… I've used Claude Code (Opus 5.5) by model satisfaction and mod.

opinions.name: Pi
opinions.point: a bit clunky to use
opinions.quote: Primarily Hermes Agent across desktop, terminal, and phone (via Telegram). I have also tried OMP but find it a bit clunky to use.

opinions.name: Hermes Agent
opinions.point: favourite tool, works well with local models
opinions.quote: I have also tried OMP but find it a bit clunky to use. Hermes tui + tmux are my favourite tools and Hermes works well with local models.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: surprisingly effective without massive token use
opinions.quote: Claude Code ($100 for business) directly from my sandbox folder with clean versions of every repo. This is surprisingly effective. I thought it would consume massive tokens, it doesn’t.

opinions.name: Gemini
opinions.point: really likes it for research and occasional questions
opinions.quote: Gemini, company-wide. I mostly use it for general research, making clip art, and occasional programming questions / technical questions. I don't use it everyday, but when I use it, I really like it.

opinions.name: GitHub Copilot
opinions.point: loves it for hands-on work, can't offload unsupervised
opinions.quote: I love working with co-pilot, but it's best for work where I need to be hands-on. I really need to be able to offload simple work… to a bot that I don't need to supervise.

opinions.name: Subagents (built-in)
opinions.point: keeps worker context clean and focused
opinions.quote: If using subagents, use the main thread for only the conversation + launching subagents… Doing so keeps the worker subagent's context clean - so it can stay laser focused on the task.

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: stopped supporting Claude, forcing a switch
opinions.quote: I used Open Code, but they stopped supporting Claude, so I was searching for something different (I had a free 20x Max plan as an open source maintainer).

opinions.name: Instinct
opinions.point: iMessage makes it easy on the go
opinions.quote: Hermes and openclaw for most routines. Dots and Pickle to call while driving. Instinct because imessage makes it easy on the go.

opinions.name: OpenRouter
opinions.point: hit walls with OpenRouter plus Cline
opinions.quote: I'm a solo developer. I'd hit walls with openrouter (sonnet/opus/sol) + cline Now I'm running qwen 3.8 FN + omp [which] has pretty much "solved" node/react coding for me

opinions.name: Cline
opinions.point: hit walls with OpenRouter plus Cline
opinions.quote: I'm a solo developer. I'd hit walls with openrouter (sonnet/opus/sol) + cline Now I'm running qwen 3.8 FN + omp [which] has pretty much "solved" node/react coding for me

opinions.name: Qwen
opinions.point: local Qwen plus omp solved node/react coding
opinions.quote: Now I'm running qwen 3.8 FN + omp + https://github.com/mattpocock/skills This combination has pretty much "solved" node/react coding for me, running locally on dual RTX 6000

opinions.name: Pi
opinions.point: with local Qwen, solved node/react coding
opinions.quote: Now I'm running qwen 3.8 FN + omp + https://github.com/mattpocock/skills This combination has pretty much "solved" node/react coding for me, running locally on dual RTX 6000

opinions.name: DSH
opinions.point: does everything needed, no more tools required
opinions.quote: DSH + 3xSpark + GLM5.3 Flash I dont think i would need anything anymore. Its doing alot more than what i did 2 years ago in within 2 months.

opinions.name: GLM
opinions.point: does everything needed, no more tools required
opinions.quote: DSH + 3xSpark + GLM5.3 Flash I dont think i would need anything anymore. Its doing alot more than what i did 2 years ago in within 2 months.

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: great, leaving only for industry regulations
opinions.quote: In the process of moving from claude code (opus 5.5 sub) to opencode… Claude code is/was great. Just need to move due to industry regulations.

opinions.name: Custom harness
opinions.point: genuinely very happy with own experimental system
opinions.quote: I built my experimental system and I'm using it. I'm genuinely very happy with it.

opinions.name: Custom harness
opinions.point: Android frontend works surprisingly well
opinions.quote: I have a custom frontend on my android running claude and antigravity CLIs with a UI built on top. Works surprisingly well. It's now about 40 % of my usage

opinions.name: OpenCode
opinions.point: works well for pretty much any task
opinions.quote: [I use] opencode 2 as the harness it works well for pretty much any specific task

opinions.name: OpenRouter
opinions.point: DeepSeek Flash via OpenRouter cheap, good, fast
opinions.quote: [I use] opencode 2 as the harness… openrouter to use deepseek flash 4.1 … insanely cheap, works amazingly well and fast

opinions.name: Claude Code
opinions.point: alarmingly tried logging into remote systems
opinions.quote: I've moved all my ssh keys into a key-agent which prompts for key use as I got alarmed by claude attempting to login to remote systems to verify things as it worked through problems.

opinions.name: Git worktrees
opinions.point: stops parallel sessions stepping on each other
opinions.quote: Worktrees have been really useful when running multiple sessions on the same repo, otherwise they can step on each others changes.
